<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p4.3" class="ltx_p">Essentially, <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> can be interpreted as the largest plausible value that the system FDR could take, given that an extremely small <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FDR}_{cal}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FDR</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FDR}_{cal}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> is observed on the calibration set at significance level <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.
If the true system FDR were to exceed this bound, then observing <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FDR}_{cal}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FDR</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FDR}_{cal}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> in a single realization would be statistically impossible at the level <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.
A formal proof of Eq. (<a href="#S3.E10" title="Equation 10 ‣ 3.4 Uncertainty Calibration for Selective Prediction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>) is provided in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Proofs ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">To rigorously constrain test-time FDR, we calibrate <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> does not exceed the risk level <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\tau}=\sup\{\tau:\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)\leq\alpha\}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">sup</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\tau}=\sup\{\tau:\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)\leq\alpha\}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p5.2" class="ltx_p">The choice of <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> maximizes the acceptance of model predictions (or minimizes the abstention rate), while maintaining marginal FDR control.
For a test sample <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{test},q_{test},B_{test}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{test},q_{test},B_{test}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> with the model prediction <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{test}^{(MLG)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{test}^{(MLG)}</annotation></semantics></math> and estimated uncertainty score <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{test}=U\left(\hat{y}_{test}^{(MLG)}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{test}=U\left(\hat{y}_{test}^{(MLG)}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, by applying the calibrated decision threshold <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>, we establish the following guarantee</p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr\left(\Pr\left(A\big(\hat{y}_{test}^{(MLG)},B^{*}_{test}\big)=0\mid u_{test}\leq\hat{\tau}\right)\leq\alpha\right)\geq 1-\delta." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≤</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr\left(\Pr\left(A\big(\hat{y}_{test}^{(MLG)},B^{*}_{test}\big)=0\mid u_{test}\leq\hat{\tau}\right)\leq\alpha\right)\geq 1-\delta.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cascading Inference.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At inference time, for each test input <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{test},q_{test})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{test},q_{test})</annotation></semantics></math>, we first estimate the model uncertainty <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{test}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{test}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then perform selective prediction and escalating:</p>
<ul id="S3.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{test}\leq\hat{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≤</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{test}\leq\hat{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the sample as “safe” and accept the prediction of the primary model.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{test}&gt;\hat{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{test}&gt;\hat{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>, we flag the sample as “risky” and escalate the input to a stronger model to enhance performance.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiment</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Experimental Settings</h3>

<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Models and Dataset</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct our experiments over 6 GUI-grounding models, including Holo1.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Company, 2025</a>)</cite>, GUI-Actor <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, UI-TARS-1.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qin et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, GTA1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>: Holo1.5-3B, Holo1.5-7B, GUI-Actor-2VL-7B, GUI-Actor-2.5VL-7B, UI-TARS-1.5-7B and GTA1-7B.
To assess reliability under high-stakes scenarios, we conduct all experiments on the challenging ScreenSpot-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>)</cite> benchmark. Additional dataset details are provided in the Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Dataset ‣ Appendix B Details of Experimental Settings ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation Metrics</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To comprehensively evaluate both the discriminative ability of UQ methods and the reliability and effectiveness of <span id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SafeGround</span>, we adopt four complementary metrics: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic (AUROC), Area Under Accuracy-Rejection Curve (AUARC), FDR, and power <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025c</a>)</cite>. AUROC measures the ability of uncertainty estimates to distinguish correct from incorrect predictions, while AUARC evaluates whether prediction accuracy improves as high-uncertainty samples are progressively rejected. FDR quantifies the proportion of incorrect predictions among the accepted samples.
Power measures the proportion of correct samples that are retained after uncertainty-based selection, relative to the total number of correct samples. More details about the metrics can be found in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Evaluation Metrics ‣ Appendix B Details of Experimental Settings ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Hyperparameters</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For uncertainty estimation, we sample each input 10 times with the decoding temperature set to 1.0 to compute the corresponding UQ score. The most likely generation <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{i}^{(\mathrm{MLG})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>MLG</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{i}^{(\mathrm{MLG})}</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained by uniformly sampling one output from the generated candidates.
Specifically, when computing UQ scores, we partition the input into patches with a patch size of 14 to obtain region-level scores <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> for uncertainty estimation.
We repeat the random calibration–test split 100 times and report the mean and standard deviation (mean<math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math>std) over all runs.
All confidence bounds are constructed at a significance level of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=0.05</annotation></semantics></math>.
For the combined uncertainty score <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\mathrm{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>COM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\mathrm{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math>, we use a fixed weighting scheme <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.6,0.2,0.2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.6,0.2,0.2)</annotation></semantics></math> across all models.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following prior work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kuhn et al., 2023a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Band et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, we evaluate the quality of uncertainty estimates using AUROC and AUARC, which measure the discriminative ability of uncertainty scores and their effectiveness for selective prediction, respectively. We compare our distribution-aware uncertainty with the probabilistic confidence (PC) baseline, defined as one minus the average token probability <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pouget et al., 2016</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> reports AUROC results across six GUI grounding models.
When PC is available, our method consistently achieves higher AUROC.
, and on Holo1.5-7B from 0.6983 to 0.7526.
For models where PC is not directly applicable (e.g., GUI-Actor variants), our method still attains strong AUROC values (up to 0.8155), demonstrating robust error discrimination under limited model access.
Overall, these results suggest that modeling the spatial distribution of grounding predictions yields more informative uncertainty signals than token-level confidence alone.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We further evaluate uncertainty quality using AUARC, which captures accuracy gains as high uncertainty predictions are progressively rejected.
As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.2 Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, our method consistently outperforms baselines across models.
For example, on Holo1.5-3B, AUARC improves from 0.6444 to 0.6576 compared to PC.
These results indicate that our uncertainty estimates are particularly effective for guiding selective prediction decisions.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.02419v2/pics/guarantee_empirical_error.png" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/106;" width="381" height="106" alt="Refer to caption">

</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Selective Prediction with FDR Guarantees</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While AUROC and AUARC evaluate the quality of uncertainty estimates, reliable deployment further requires translating these scores into principled decision rules with explicit risk guarantees.
We therefore study selective prediction under false discovery rate (FDR) control.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">FDR Control Guarantee</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each uncertainty method and risk level, we calibrate a decision threshold on the calibration set using the Clopper–Pearson upper confidence bound <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Clopper and Pearson, 1934</a>)</cite>, ensuring that the test-time FDR does not exceed the specified risk level with high probability.
Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.2 Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> illustrates the empirical FDR on the test set across various user-specified risk levels (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>). Notably, the evaluated risk levels start from a minimum attainable value. This arises because the intrinsic limitations of the base model and the imperfect discriminative power of uncertainty estimates may cause some incorrect predictions to receive relatively low uncertainty scores, making them inseparable from correct ones by thresholding.
As a result, very stringent FDR requirements may be infeasible to satisfy, as no decision threshold can meet the risk constraint under such conditions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>.
Importantly, this does not undermine the safety guarantee, as the calibration stage explicitly determines whether a user-specified risk level is achievable prior to deployment, providing a principled fail-safe mechanism for high-stakes interactions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The results in Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.2 Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> show that for all tested models (e.g., Holo1.5, UI-TARS), the actual FDR is consistently bounded below the theoretical upper bound. This empirically verifies that <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SafeGround</span> provides rigorous safety guarantees, ensuring that, with high probability, the error rate among accepted predictions is controlled at the specified level.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Power Comparison</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to FDR, we report power to further characterize the effectiveness of selective prediction. Higher power indicates that the uncertainty estimates more precisely identify truly risky cases, allowing the system to retain a larger set of reliable predictions without violating the target FDR. Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> compares the power of our method <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\text{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mtext>COM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\text{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math> versus the PC baseline under identical risk levels.
Across the evaluated models, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\text{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mtext>COM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\text{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math> demonstrates superior robustness, particularly at strict risk levels (e.g., 0.38) where PC often fails to yield valid predictions.
Notably, the minimum attainable risk level at which PC can satisfy the FDR constraint is consistently higher than that of <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\text{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mtext>COM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\text{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating a narrower feasible operating range for PC.
<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\text{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mtext>COM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\text{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math> consistently outperforms PC, retaining a significantly larger volume of correct responses.
These results indicate that <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\text{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mtext>COM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\text{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math> is systematically less conservative than PC: it accepts a larger fraction of correct predictions while still satisfying the same FDR constraint.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Cascading Inference</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we study the system-level benefits of uncertainty-aware decision making in a cascaded inference setting.
Given that powerful external models (e.g., Gemini) often incur latency and financial costs, our goal is to improve system accuracy by selectively invoking stronger models when the uncertainty of the base model exceeds a calibrated threshold.
Specifically, we fix the calibration split ratio to 0.2 and use the remaining 80% of the data as the test set to evaluate the cascaded system.
At test time, predictions with uncertainty scores below or equal to the threshold are handled by the primary local grounding model, while high-uncertainty cases are deferred to the stronger expert model, Gemini-3-pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> reports the accuracy of uncertainty-aware Gemini cascading under different risk levels. Across a wide range of feasible risk levels, the proposed approach consistently improves system accuracy over both Gemini-only inference and the base models, demonstrating the effectiveness of uncertainty-aware cascading. At relatively small risk levels, uncertainty-aware cascading yields substantial accuracy gains. For instance, with Holo1.5-7B at risk level <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.34" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.34</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.34</annotation></semantics></math>, the system achieves <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58.66\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>58.66</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58.66\%</annotation></semantics></math> accuracy, outperforming Gemini-only inference by <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.38\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.38</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.38\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
As the risk level increases, the improvement gradually diminishes, since fewer high-uncertainty samples are deferred to Gemini, and the system behavior approaches that of the base model.
The effect is more pronounced for models such as Holo1.5-3B and UI-TARS-1.5-7B, where uncertainty-aware cascading improves accuracy by more than <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>13</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13\%</annotation></semantics></math> over the base models at relatively small risk levels.
We also report the cascading rate in Figure <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.4 Cascading Inference ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, i.e., the fraction of test samples deferred to Gemini.
As the risk level increases, the cascading rate consistently decreases across all models, indicating that fewer uncertain cases are escalated to the expert model.
This reflects the inherent trade-off between accuracy and expert invocation cost in uncertainty-aware cascading.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.02419v2/pics/abstention_rates.png" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:467/236;" width="467" height="236" alt="Refer to caption">

</figure>

</figure></div></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Sensitivity Analyses</h3>

<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sampling Efficiency</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We investigate the trade-off between computational cost and estimation quality by varying the sample count <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> and measuring the resulting AUROC and AUARC. As shown in Figure <a href="#S4.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 4.4 Cascading Inference ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, increasing the sample size from <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=10</annotation></semantics></math> yields a improvement for both metrics, indicating that the proposed uncertainty estimates are already effective with a small number of samples. In contrast, further increasing <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> from 10 to 15 leads to only marginal changes. Based on this trade-off between performance and computational cost, we set <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=10</annotation></semantics></math> as the default sampling size in all experiments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Ablation of Uncertainty Components</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We analyze the contribution of individual uncertainty components, <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{TA}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{TA}</annotation></semantics></math> , <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{IE}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{IE}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{CD}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{CD}</annotation></semantics></math>, across different GUI grounding models.
As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Ablation of Uncertainty Components ‣ 4.5 Sensitivity Analyses ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, the most informative uncertainty cue is model-dependent.
On GTA1, <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{TA}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{TA}</annotation></semantics></math> is the strongest single signal, whereas for GUI-Actor-2VL and Holo1.5, <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{CD}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{CD}</annotation></semantics></math> is more effective, and <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{TA}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{TA}</annotation></semantics></math> alone is insufficient.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Across all models, no single component consistently dominates.
<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{COM}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{COM}</annotation></semantics></math> achieves stable performance in all settings, and removing the dominant component for a given model leads to a clear drop in both AUROC and AUARC.
This indicates that combining complementary cues yields a more robust, model-agnostic uncertainty estimate for selective prediction.
Additional robustness analyses with respect to the uncertainty weighting are provided in the Appendix <a href="#A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Sensitivity to Uncertainty Weighting. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="S4.T4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">

</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sensitivity to Calibration-Test Split Ratio</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further study the sensitivity of our method to the calibration–test split ratio when using the combined uncertainty measure <math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\text{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mtext>COM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\text{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Specifically, we vary the proportion of data allocated to the calibration set while keeping the target risk level fixed, and evaluate the resulting empirical FDR on the test set.
As shown in Figure <a href="#S4.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 4.4 Cascading Inference ‣ 4 Experiment ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, across a wide range of split ratios, the empirical FDR achieved by all three models remains consistently below the target upper bound.
These results suggest that our approach does not rely on a carefully tuned split ratio and can be applied robustly in practical settings.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SafeGround</span>, an uncertainty-aware framework that enables reliable and risk controlled GUI grounding under limited model access.
By modeling spatial uncertainty from stochastic grounding samples, <span id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SafeGround</span> captures distributional signals that go beyond point predictions and provide effective discrimination between correct and incorrect predictions.
Based on uncertainty estimation, we further calibrate decision thresholds with finite-sample guarantees, supporting deployment-time decision making in high-stakes GUI interactions.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that <span id="S5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SafeGround</span> achieves accurate uncertainty discrimination, rigorous FDR control, and improved system-level performance through selective prediction and cascading inference. We hope this work provides a principled way for deploying GUI agents with safety guarantees.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper introduces <span id="Sx1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SafeGround</span>, a framework that significantly enhances the reliability and safety of autonomous GUI agents. By providing the first principled method for uncertainty quantification in GUI grounding with finite-sample statistical guarantees, our work addresses a critical bottleneck in the real-world deployment of visual agents, the risk of high-stakes, irreversible errors (e.g., erroneous financial transactions). Beyond improving individual model reliability, the proposed selective deferral mechanism demonstrates that local models, when combined with uncertainty-aware cascading to powerful external experts, can achieve superior system-level accuracy with substantially reduced computational costs.
This research provides a foundational step toward trustworthy human-AI interaction in digital environments, ensuring that automated systems “know when they don’t know” and make conservative decisions under ambiguous conditions.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="Ax1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix">Limitation</h2>

<div id="Ax1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our uncertainty estimation relies on the variability in the sampled predictions to characterize spatial ambiguity.
For highly deterministic models with limited sampling diversity, the resulting spatial distributions may be less informative.
Despite these limitations, <span id="Ax1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SafeGround</span> provides a general and principled foundation for uncertainty-aware GUI grounding.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Proofs</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we provide a compelete proof that the upper confidence bound <math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> defined in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E9" title="Equation 9 ‣ 3.4 Uncertainty Calibration for Selective Prediction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>) satisfies the statistical guarantee in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E9" title="Equation 9 ‣ 3.4 Uncertainty Calibration for Selective Prediction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>).
Recall <math id="A1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)=\sup\{R:\Pr(\mathrm{Bin}(n,R)\leq X)\geq\delta\}" display="inline" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">sup</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Bin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)=\sup\{R:\Pr(\mathrm{Bin}(n,R)\leq X)\geq\delta\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="n=\sum_{i}^{N}\mathbf{1}\{u_{i}\leq\tau\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo encoding="application/x-tex">n=\sum_{i}^{N}\mathbf{1}\{u_{i}\leq\tau\}</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of accepted calibration samples, and <math id="A1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=\sum_{i}^{N}\mathbf{1}\{u_{i}\leq\tau,A(\hat{y}_{i}^{(MLG)},B_{i}^{*})=0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mn>𝟏</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=\sum_{i}^{N}\mathbf{1}\{u_{i}\leq\tau,A(\hat{y}_{i}^{(MLG)},B_{i}^{*})=0\}</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of accepted incorrect calibration samples.
In general, <math id="A1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Bin}(n,R)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Bin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Bin}(n,R)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the random variable representing the number of successes in <math id="A1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> Bernoulli trials when the system success probability is <math id="A1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>.
In our setting, it corresponds to the random variable counting the number of errors among <math id="A1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> samples when the system FDR is <math id="A1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> under a given threshold <math id="A1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We define the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the random variable <math id="A1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{R}(\tau)=\frac{\mathrm{Bin}(n;R(\tau))}{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>Bin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{R}(\tau)=\frac{\mathrm{Bin}(n;R(\tau))}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, corresponding to the error rate over any <math id="A1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> accepted samples when the system FDR is <math id="A1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math>, as</p>
<table id="A1.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CDF}\big(r\mid R(\tau)\big)=\Pr\big(\hat{R}(\tau)\leq r\mid R(\tau)\big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>CDF</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CDF}\big(r\mid R(\tau)\big)=\Pr\big(\hat{R}(\tau)\leq r\mid R(\tau)\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">By the definition of <math id="A1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</p>
<table id="A1.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CDF}\left(\frac{X}{n}\mid\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)\right)=\delta." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>CDF</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CDF}\left(\frac{X}{n}\mid\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)\right)=\delta.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(\tau)&gt;\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(\tau)&gt;\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CDF}\left(\frac{X}{n}\mid R(\tau)\right)\leq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>CDF</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CDF}\left(\frac{X}{n}\mid R(\tau)\right)\leq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then, we have</p>
<table id="A1.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

&amp;\geq 1-\Pr\left(\mathrm{CDF}\left(\frac{X}{n}\mid R(\tau)\right)\leq\delta\right)\end{split}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtable columnspacing="0pt" displaystyle="true" fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation &amp;\geq 1-\Pr\left(\mathrm{CDF}\left(\frac{X}{n}\mid R(\tau)\right)\leq\delta\right)\end{split}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">We further the Inverse Cumulative Distribution Function (ICDF):</p>
