</table>
<p id="A1.p2.5" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CDF}\left(\frac{X}{n}\mid R(\tau)\right)\leq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>CDF</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CDF}\left(\frac{X}{n}\mid R(\tau)\right)\leq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{X}{n}\leq\mathrm{CDF}^{-1}\big(\delta\mid R(\tau)\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mi>CDF</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{X}{n}\leq\mathrm{CDF}^{-1}\big(\delta\mid R(\tau)\big)</annotation></semantics></math>.
We then obtain</p>
<table id="A1.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr\left(R(\tau)\leq\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)\right)\geq 1-\Pr\left(\frac{X}{n}\leq\mathrm{CDF}^{-1}\big(\delta\mid R(\tau)\big)\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mi>CDF</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr\left(R(\tau)\leq\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)\right)\geq 1-\Pr\left(\frac{X}{n}\leq\mathrm{CDF}^{-1}\big(\delta\mid R(\tau)\big)\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.p2.6" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="A1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{X}{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{X}{n}</annotation></semantics></math> is exactly the empirical error rate observed over the <math id="A1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> accepted samples in the calibration set, the probability that it is less than or equal to <math id="A1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CDF}^{-1}\big(\delta\mid R(\tau)\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>CDF</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CDF}^{-1}\big(\delta\mid R(\tau)\big)</annotation></semantics></math> does not exceed <math id="A1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.
Finally, we conclude</p>
<table id="A1.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr\left(R(\tau)\leq\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)\right)\geq 1-\delta." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>FDR</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr\left(R(\tau)\leq\hat{\mathrm{FDR}}_{1-\delta}^{upper}(\tau)\right)\geq 1-\delta.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.p2.7" class="ltx_p">In this way, we obtain an upper bound on the system FDR at threshold <math id="A1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> with at least <math id="A1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math> confidence.
At test time, by the exchangeability condition, we provide marginal guarantees of FDR control.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Details of Experimental Settings</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Dataset</h3>

<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ScreenSpot-Pro</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">ScreenSpot-Pro consists of 1581 UI screenshots paired with natural language instructions that refer to target UI elements on the screen.
Each target is annotated as a spatial region rather than a single point.
Compared to earlier GUI grounding benchmarks, ScreenSpot-Pro features higher visual complexity, denser UI layouts, and more fine-grained distinctions between neighboring elements, making it particularly suitable for studying uncertainty-aware grounding.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Evaluation Metrics</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate uncertainty estimation quality and selective prediction performance using four complementary metrics: AUROC, AUARC, FDR, and power.
All metrics are defined with respect to the admission function
<math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A(\hat{y},B^{*})\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(\hat{y},B^{*})\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> introduced in Section <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Problem Formulation and Notations ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, which indicates whether a grounding prediction is admissible.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic (AUROC)</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(\hat{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(\hat{y})</annotation></semantics></math> denote an uncertainty score, where larger values indicate higher uncertainty.
AUROC measures how well <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(\hat{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(\hat{y})</annotation></semantics></math> separates inadmissible predictions from admissible ones.
Formally, AUROC is the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve obtained by thresholding <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(\hat{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(\hat{y})</annotation></semantics></math> to predict whether <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A(\hat{y},B^{*})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(\hat{y},B^{*})=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
A higher AUROC indicates stronger discriminative ability of the uncertainty estimate.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Area Under Accuracy-Rejection Curve (AUARC)</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">AUARC evaluates selective prediction behavior by measuring how accuracy changes as predictions with high uncertainty are rejected.
Let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\tau}=\{i:U(\hat{y}_{i})\leq\tau\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\tau}=\{i:U(\hat{y}_{i})\leq\tau\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the set of accepted samples under threshold <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>.
The accuracy at <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as</p>
<table id="A2.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Acc}(\tau)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{S}_{\tau}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}_{\tau}}A(\hat{y}_{i},B_{i}^{*})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Acc}(\tau)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{S}_{\tau}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}_{\tau}}A(\hat{y}_{i},B_{i}^{*}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">In practice, <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is chosen to correspond to a target rejection rate, and AUARC is computed as the area under the curve of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Acc}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Acc}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> as a function of the rejection rate.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">False Discovery Rate (FDR)</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under a given uncertainty threshold <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, the false discovery rate is defined as</p>
<table id="A2.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FDR}(\tau)=\frac{\sum_{i}\mathbb{I}\big(U(\hat{y}_{i})\leq\tau\big)\,\mathbb{I}\big(A(\hat{y}_{i},B_{i}^{*})=0\big)}{\sum_{i}\mathbb{I}\big(U(\hat{y}_{i})\leq\tau\big)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>FDR</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝕀</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FDR}(\tau)=\frac{\sum_{i}\mathbb{I}\big(U(\hat{y}_{i})\leq\tau\big)\,\mathbb{I}\big(A(\hat{y}_{i},B_{i}^{*})=0\big)}{\sum_{i}\mathbb{I}\big(U(\hat{y}_{i})\leq\tau\big)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">FDR quantifies the proportion of inadmissible predictions among all accepted predictions and serves as the primary risk metric controlled by <span id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SafeGround</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Power</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Power measures the proportion of correct predictions retained by selective prediction under a risk constraint and is defined as:</p>
<table id="A2.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Power}(\tau)=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}\big(U(\hat{y}_{i})\leq\tau\big)\mathbb{I}\big(A(\hat{y}_{i},B_{i}^{*})=1\big)}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}\big(A(\hat{y}_{i},B_{i}^{*})=1\big)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Power</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝕀</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Power}(\tau)=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}\big(U(\hat{y}_{i})\leq\tau\big)\mathbb{I}\big(A(\hat{y}_{i},B_{i}^{*})=1\big)}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}\big(A(\hat{y}_{i},B_{i}^{*})=1\big)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Higher power indicates that more correct predictions are retained while satisfying the specified FDR constraint.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Spatial Region Construction</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given an input image–instruction pair <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,q)</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain a set of <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> sampled grounding predictions
<math id="A2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{S}=\{\hat{y}^{(i)}=(x^{(i)},y^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=\{\hat{y}^{(i)}=(x^{(i)},y^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math> via stochastic decoding.
To lift these point-wise samples into a spatial distribution, we discretize the screen into a fixed
<math id="A2.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\times W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\times W</annotation></semantics></math> grid of patches and map each sampled coordinate to its corresponding patch.
Let <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{u,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{u,v}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the number of samples falling into patch <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(u,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u,v)</annotation></semantics></math>.
We then normalize the resulting count map to obtain a spatial probability distribution</p>
<table id="A2.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{u,v}=\frac{C_{u,v}}{\sum_{u^{\prime},v^{\prime}}C_{u^{\prime},v^{\prime}}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{u,v}=\frac{C_{u,v}}{\sum_{u^{\prime},v^{\prime}}C_{u^{\prime},v^{\prime}}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which serves as an empirical estimate of the model’s predictive density over the output space.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Region Extraction</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To identify object-level grounding hypotheses, we first filter low-density patches using an
instance-adaptive threshold.
Specifically, let <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\max}=\max_{u,v}P_{u,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\max}=\max_{u,v}P_{u,v}</annotation></semantics></math>, and retain only patches satisfying
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{u,v}&gt;\beta P_{\max}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{u,v}&gt;\beta P_{\max}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> is a fixed ratio (set to <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math> in our experiments, following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>).
We then group spatially adjacent retained patches (using 4-connected neighborhood) into connected components.
This yields a set of disjoint regions
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}=\{R_{m}\}_{m=1}^{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}=\{R_{m}\}_{m=1}^{M}</annotation></semantics></math>, each corresponding to a plausible grounding target.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Region Scoring</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each region <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute a region-level score</p>
<table id="A2.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{m}=\frac{1}{|R_{m}|}\sum_{(u,v)\in R_{m}}P_{u,v}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></munder><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{m}=\frac{1}{|R_{m}|}\sum_{(u,v)\in R_{m}}P_{u,v},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">i.e., the average probability density within the region.
This score reflects the relative support assigned to the region by the sampled predictions while
remaining invariant to region size.
The resulting region scores <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{S_{m}\}_{m=1}^{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{S_{m}\}_{m=1}^{M}</annotation></semantics></math> are subsequently normalized and used to compute
the uncertainty metrics described in Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Uncertainty Quantification ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">

<div id="alg1.l5" class="ltx_listingline">

</div>
<div id="alg1.l6" class="ltx_listingline">

<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">

            <span id="alg1.l7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <math id="alg1.l7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">to</span> <math id="alg1.l7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l7.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>



</div>
<div id="alg1.l8" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">8:</span></span>
            
            
             Map <math id="alg1.l8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}^{(k)}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}^{(k)}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> to patch index <math id="alg1.l8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(u,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u,v)</annotation></semantics></math> and set <math id="alg1.l8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{u,v}\leftarrow C_{u,v}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{u,v}\leftarrow C_{u,v}+1</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l9" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l9.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">9:</span></span>
            
            
            <span id="alg1.l9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg1.l9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l10" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l10.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">10:</span></span>
            
            
            Normalize to density <math id="alg1.l10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{u,v}\leftarrow\frac{C_{u,v}}{\sum_{u^{\prime},v^{\prime}}C_{u^{\prime},v^{\prime}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><msub><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub></mstyle><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{u,v}\leftarrow\frac{C_{u,v}}{\sum_{u^{\prime},v^{\prime}}C_{u^{\prime},v^{\prime}}}</annotation></semantics></math>

<div id="alg1.l27" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l27.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">27:</span></span>
            
            
            <math id="alg1.l27.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="n\leftarrow\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}\{u_{(j)}\leq\tau\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo rspace="0.111em" stretchy="false">←</mo><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\leftarrow\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}\{u_{(j)}\leq\tau\}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l27.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;">(number of accepted samples)
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l28" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l28.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">28:</span></span>
            
            
            <math id="alg1.l28.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="X\leftarrow\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}\{u_{(j)}\leq\tau\land err_{(j)}=1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo rspace="0.111em" stretchy="false">←</mo><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>∧</mo><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\leftarrow\sum_{j=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}\{u_{(j)}\leq\tau\land err_{(j)}=1\}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l28.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;">(number of errors among accepted)
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l29" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l29.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">29:</span></span>
            
            
            <span id="alg1.l29.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Compute Clopper–Pearson upper bound:</span> <math id="alg1.l29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{UCB}\leftarrow\mathrm{BetaInv}(1-\delta;\,X+1,\,n-X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>UCB</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>BetaInv</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{UCB}\leftarrow\mathrm{BetaInv}(1-\delta;\,X+1,\,n-X)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l30" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l30.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">30:</span></span>
            
            
            <span id="alg1.l30.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span> <math id="alg1.l30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{UCB}\leq\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>UCB</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{UCB}\leq\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l30.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">then</span>



</div>
<div id="alg1.l31" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l31.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">31:</span></span>
            
            
             Update <math id="alg1.l31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\tau}\leftarrow\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\tau}\leftarrow\tau</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l32" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l32.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">32:</span></span>

<div id="alg1.l33" class="ltx_listingline">

<div id="alg1.l34" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l34.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">34:</span></span>
            
            
           <span id="alg1.l34.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span> <math id="alg1.l34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\tau}=\texttt{NULL}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">NULL</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\tau}=\texttt{NULL}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l34.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">then</span>



</div>

            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l35.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">35:</span></span>
            
            
            <span id="alg1.l35.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Return</span> “The target risk level <math id="alg1.l35.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> is unattainable under calibration.”

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Prompt Template</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure a fair and reliable evaluation of large vision–language models on GUI grounding, we adopt a strictly constrained prompt template for Gemini in the ScreenSpot-Pro benchmark, as illustrated in Figure <a href="#A4.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix D Prompt Template ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, <a href="#A4.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Appendix D Prompt Template ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Additional Experimental Results</h2>

<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sensitivity to Sampling Temperature.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further examine the sensitivity of the proposed uncertainty measures to the sampling temperature used during stochastic decoding.
Table <a href="#A6.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Sensitivity to Sampling Temperature. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> and Table <a href="#A6.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Sensitivity to Sampling Temperature. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> report AUROC and AUARC results on Holo1.5-3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Company, 2025</a>)</cite> under different temperature settings.
As the temperature increases, <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{IE}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{IE}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{CD}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{CD}</annotation></semantics></math> become more informative, reflected by consistent gains in AUROC.
In contrast, margin-based uncertainty exhibits relatively limited sensitivity to temperature changes.
<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{COM}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{COM}</annotation></semantics></math> shows a dependence on the sampling temperature, reflecting its ability to adapt to changes in the diversity and dispersion of stochastic predictions, while remaining competitive across the evaluated temperature range.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5: </span>AUROC of different uncertainty measures on Holo1.5-3B under varying sampling temperatures.</figcaption>

<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sensitivity to Uncertainty Weighting.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We examine the sensitivity of the proposed framework to the weighting scheme used in the combined uncertainty score <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\mathrm{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>COM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\mathrm{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Starting from the default setting <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.6,0.2,0.2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.6,0.2,0.2)</annotation></semantics></math>, we evaluate several alternative weighting configurations that moderately vary the relative contributions of the three uncertainty components, while keeping the weights normalized.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Specifically, we consider the following weighting configurations for the combined uncertainty score <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\mathrm{COM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>COM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\mathrm{COM}}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<ul id="A6.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">v1:</span> <math id="A6.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.34,0.33,0.33)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.34</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.33</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.33</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.34,0.33,0.33)</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">v2:</span> <math id="A6.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.2,0.2,0.6)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.2,0.2,0.6)</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">v3:</span> <math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.2,0.6,0.2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.2,0.6,0.2)</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">v4:</span> <math id="A6.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.5,0.25,0.25)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.5,0.25,0.25)</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">v5:</span> <math id="A6.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.25,0.25,0.5)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.25,0.25,0.5)</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">v6:</span> <math id="A6.I1.i6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.25,0.5,0.25)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.25,0.5,0.25)</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">original:</span> <math id="A6.I1.i7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.6,0.2,0.2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{CD},w_{IE},w_{TA})=(0.6,0.2,0.2)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Figure <a href="#A6.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ Sensitivity to Uncertainty Weighting. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>, <a href="#A6.F16" title="Figure 16 ‣ Sensitivity to Uncertainty Weighting. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>, <a href="#A6.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ Sensitivity to Uncertainty Weighting. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>, <a href="#A6.F19" title="Figure 19 ‣ Sensitivity to Uncertainty Weighting. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>, <a href="#A6.F17" title="Figure 17 ‣ Sensitivity to Uncertainty Weighting. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>, <a href="#A6.F20" title="Figure 20 ‣ Sensitivity to Uncertainty Weighting. ‣ Appendix F Additional Experimental Results ‣ SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>, across all evaluated models, both AUROC and AUARC exhibit only minor fluctuations under different weighting schemes. These results indicate that the proposed uncertainty aggregation is robust to moderate changes in the weighting scheme, supporting the use of a fixed, model-agnostic combination in practice.</p>
</div>
